newsitem.title: ITALY: IBCA affirms Italy Banca Regionale Europea ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA affirms Italy Banca Regionale Europea ratings.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Wednesday it affirmed Italian Banca Regionale Europea's long-term rating at A and short-term rating at A1.
In a statement received in Milan, IBCA said the individual and legal ratings remained unchanged at B and 4 respectively.
"Banca Regionale Europea (BRE) benefits from larges volumes of cheap customer deposits obtained from its deep rooted network around the provinces of Cuneo and Pavia," IBCA said.
Those volumes of customer deposits enabled BRE to obtain a relatively high net interest margin on its customer business, IBCA said.
"Furthermore its healthy asset quality has ensured that loan loss provisions remained stable over the past couple of years," it said.

"Although overheads have been affected by the merger of the two banks which made up BRE (Cassa di Risparmio di Cuneo and Banca del Monte di Lombardia), costs are expected to decrease steadily over the next three years," it said.
"The bank's cost/income ratio nevertheless remains below average in Italy," it said.
"BRE is well capitalised with an end-1995 EU total capital ratio of 25.05 percent, of which 24.07 percent was tier 1."
